entries.content: `make lint` runs `uv run --only-group=dev ruff check .`, `ruff format . --check`, `pyproject-fmt pyproject.toml --check`, and `djade --target-version 6.0 --check`. ruff enforces line length 120 and flags W391 (extra newline at EOF), auto-fixable via `ruff check --fix`. If `ruff format` says files would be reformatted, run `make lint-fix` and then rerun `make lint`.

make lint runs ruff check, ruff format --check, pyproject-fmt --check, and djade --target-version 6.0 --check on templates. A CI lint failure is usually just ruff format wanting files collapsed onto single lines; fix with `uv run --only-group=dev ruff format <files>`.

observations.content: `make lint` composes `ruff check .`, `ruff format . --check`, `pyproject-fmt pyproject.toml --check`, and `djade --target-version 6.0 --check` (which also covers templates); ruff's W391 extra-newline-at-EOF violation is auto-fixable via `ruff check --fix`, and a CI lint failure is usually just `ruff format` wanting files reformatted — fix with `make lint-fix` (or `uv run --only-group=dev ruff format <files>`) and rerun `make lint`.

content_must_state.o1: both that ruff's W391 extra-newline-at-EOF violation is auto-fixable via `ruff check --fix`, and that a CI lint failure from reformatting can be fixed with `make lint-fix` or `ruff format`

observations.content: Reuse existing shared classifiers and helpers before adding new error-detection logic.

entries.content: Django test client with `enforce_csrf_csrf_checks=True` can verify CSRF enforcement on session-auth routes (e.g., POST /api/chat/cancel): without X-CSRFToken → 403, with token → 200. Use sync `Client` not `AsyncClient` to avoid sqlite :memory: contention in async fixtures.

MCPServerForm is a ModelForm whose is_valid() runs validate_unique and hits the DB, so any test calling form.is_valid() needs @pytest.mark.django_db (e.g. test_user_scoped_form_rejects_hostname_resolving_to_private was missing it).

observations.content: A resolved production issue points to `daiv/core/checkpointer.py:241` and raises `NotImplementedError: Message as a sequence must be (role string, template)`. It was resolved with 6 occurrences and 1 impacted user.

entries.content: The daiv Sentry project's environment-tagging is historically a no-op: filtering by environment:production can return false negatives. When triaging, run the unresolved-issues query without the environment filter (or verify env-tagged results against an unfiltered query) to avoid missing issues.

entries.content: The Sentry org slug for the `daiv-sandbox` project is `daiv` (e.g. `organizationSlug=daiv`). `sentry_find_projects` returns only the project slug with no org info, and there is no `find_organizations` tool available, so the org slug must be guessed; `daiv` is the working value.

observations.content: The Sentry organization slug for the `daiv-sandbox` project is `srtab` (matches the GitHub org `srtab/daiv-sandbox`). There is no `find_organizations` tool exposed by the Sentry MCP server, and `sentry_find_projects` returns only the project slug without org info.

content_must_state.o1: that the Sentry org slug for `daiv-sandbox` is `srtab`

observations.content: When validating URL paths for security in this codebase, `urllib.parse.urlparse` silently strips `\n`/`\r` from the path (e.g. `urlparse('/uploads/abc\n/x').path` returns `/uploads/abc/x`), so a control-character check on the parsed path misses CR/LF injection. Control-character validation must be applied to the raw input string before parsing.

ninja's AuthRateThrottle rate strings must use the short unit `min` (e.g. `"30/min"`), NOT `minute` — `"30/minute"` raises `ValueError: Invalid rate format` at import time in ninja/throttling.py, which crashes the whole `chat.api.views` module and cascades into confusing downstream failures like "Database access not allowed" in unrelated tests. If you see that error, check the throttle rate string first.

daiv/memory/consolidation.py emits a by-design `logger.error` budget-eviction audit log (message-only, no stacktrace) like "consolidation: evicted N of M entries for repo ... to fit the ... render budget". This is intentionally routed to Sentry as the observability signal for the memory render-budget mechanism — such issues must NOT be resolved/ignored, even though they look like noise.

A recurring Sentry issue ("consolidation: evicted N of M entries ... to fit the 200 line / 10240 byte render budget") is a by-design audit log emitted from `daiv/memory/consolidation.py:183-191` when a consolidation round overflows the render budget. It has no stacktrace and should be classified as Noise/by-design in triage without fetching events.

content_must_state.o1: that this recurring Sentry issue (the memory-consolidation budget-eviction log) is a by-design audit log, not a defect, and should not be resolved or ignored

entries.content: `make lint` is the main CI gate; it covers repo lint checks and includes the egress-proxy sidecar Python 3.13 parse check. Other verified Makefile targets include `make test`, `make lint-typing`, `make run`, and `make build-egress-proxy`.

The egress proxy sidecar vendors `daiv_sandbox/egress/policy.py`, `constants.py`, and `addon.py` into its Docker build and runs them under mitmproxy's Python 3.13. Avoid Python 3.14-only syntax in those files or the addon can fail at import time and fail open.

observations.content: `daiv_sandbox/sessions.py` and `daiv_sandbox/egress/manager.py` have a circular import; the established workaround is a local import inside methods (e.g., `_get_egress_env`, `_resume_egress`). New code touching both modules should follow the same local-import pattern rather than adding a top-level import.

entries.content: `sentry_get_sentry_resource` is available for fetching a Sentry resource by URL or ID.

observations.content: The Sentry MCP `sentry_search_events` tool in this environment returns events WITHOUT `stacktrace`/`exception` content even when those fields are requested in `fields`. To obtain the full stacktrace for an issue, call `sentry_get_sentry_resource` on the issue URL instead — it returns a detailed stacktrace plus culprit and code-location info.

entries.content: The daiv-sandbox Sentry project (org slug 'srtab') has no 'production' environment tag; 'is:unresolved environment:production' returns zero results. Use the broader 'is:unresolved' query (no environment filter) as the baseline for triage on this project.
In this environment, prefer `sentry_search_events` for event lookup; `sentry_search_issue_events` was not exposed.
Useful Sentry triage tools here include `sentry_find_projects`, `sentry_search_issues`, `sentry_search_events`, and `sentry_get_sentry_resource`.

observations.content: Egress trust boundary: each session's internal network is created with `internal=True`; the sandbox container is attached only to that internal network, and only the proxy sidecar gets a second NIC on the external egress network. This is what keeps the sandbox from reaching the internet directly, regardless of proxy state.

The Sentry project `daiv-sandbox` has no `production` environment tag, so the default `environment:production` filter from the sentry-triage skill returns nothing. Use the broad `is:unresolved` query without an environment filter when triaging this project. The project resolves under org slug `srtab`.
Editing code and passing tests or lint locally is not the end of a task — always commit and push your changes to actually deliver them.

In this environment, `tool_search` did not expose `sentry_search_issue_events`; the available event-related tool was `sentry_search_events`, and `sentry_get_sentry_resource` was also available for fetching a Sentry resource by URL or ID.

In this org's Sentry MCP setup, `sentry_search_issue_events` is NOT exposed — to fetch a representative event for an issue, call `sentry_get_sentry_resource` with the issue URL instead. Also, `sentry_search_issues` rejects short period forms like `1d`; pass `24h` (or `7d`) as the period.
